description_ru: Юмористический рассказ о попытке собрать шкаф из магазина без слов в инструкции и о запасных винтиках, которые остались лишними.
text:
Last Saturday I decided to build a wardrobe. This was not a sensible decision, but it seemed like a good one at the time. The wardrobe had arrived in a flat cardboard box the size of a coffin, and the picture on the front showed a smiling couple holding a hammer and looking extremely relaxed. "Assembly time: ninety minutes," said the label. I thought that I would be finished by lunch, and I even promised my wife that she could hang her coats before dinner.

The first problem was the box itself. It took me twenty minutes to open it, because it had been taped by somebody who clearly hated me. Inside there were forty-two wooden boards, three bags of small metal objects, a tiny tool shaped like a letter L, and a booklet with no words. The booklet contained only drawings of a small man who seemed to be having a terrible time. In the first picture he was smiling. By picture nine he was crying, and in picture fourteen he was lying on the floor with a board on his head. I felt a strange connection with him.

I laid out the boards across the living room and started with step one. It said, "Attach part A to part B using screw 12." This sounded easy until I discovered that part A and part B looked exactly the same, and that there were two kinds of screw 12. One was slightly longer than the other, but I could only tell when I had already used the wrong one. If I had been more patient, I would have checked, but patience is not one of my talents. I pushed the screw in, and the board gave a small crack, like a bone.

After an hour I had built what looked like a small, unhappy bookcase. I knew that it was wrong, because it had no door and a mysterious extra shelf. I looked at the picture again. The small man had put the shelf on the inside, not on the outside, which I had missed. I took everything apart and started again. By this time, my wife had come to see how I was doing. She looked at the boards on the floor and the small pile of screws on the carpet and asked, in the voice that she uses with small children, "Would you like some help?" I said that I was fine.

The second hour was better, and for a short time I believed that I could actually finish. I had learned the secret of the instructions: you must ignore the words, which do not exist, and trust the arrows. By two o'clock the frame was standing, the doors were hanging, and I felt like a master builder. I made a cup of tea and admired my work. That was a mistake, because I then noticed that the doors were crooked. One of them was open by about five centimetres and would not close, no matter how hard I pushed.

I spent another forty minutes trying to repair it. I pulled, I pushed, and I hit the wardrobe gently with a hammer, which only made the sound of a dull drum. Finally I realised that one of the doors was upside down. The handle, which should have been at the side, was at the bottom, so that anyone who wanted to open the wardrobe would have to kneel like a person in church. I sighed, took the door off, turned it around and put it on again. This time it closed with a perfect click, and I made a small victory dance in the living room.

Unfortunately, the dance was a little too enthusiastic. As I turned around, my elbow hit the side of the wardrobe, and the whole thing leaned slowly forward like a tired person. I caught it just in time, but one of the shelves slid out, and it landed on my foot. I will not repeat what I said, but my neighbour, who was working in his garden, told me later that he had learned three new words. My wife brought frozen peas.

At six o'clock I counted the leftovers. There were six screws, two small wooden pins and a metal piece that I did not recognise. I looked at the picture, and the small man had none of them. I decided that the manufacturer had made a mistake and that the wardrobe was probably safer without them. I put them in a jar and placed it on a high shelf with the other leftovers from earlier projects. It already contained leftovers from the bookcase, the table and a chair.

The wardrobe now stands in our bedroom. It leans slightly to the left, and when you open the right door, you can hear a sound like a small, worried bird. My wife has hung all her coats inside, and so far nothing has fallen. She says that it has character, and I have decided to agree. If anybody asks, I tell them that I built it myself, and I have never lied less. Next week, however, I will buy something that comes already assembled, and I will pay the extra money without complaining.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Кончик языка слегка между зубами, воздух проходит без голоса; не заменяйте на «с» или «ф».
Губы округлены и вытянуты вперёд, зубов не касаются; это не русское «в».
Спинка языка прижата к нёбу, звук идёт через нос; в конце -ing не добавляйте «г».
Ударный слог длиннее, громче и выше по тону; остальные слоги сокращаются, особенно в длинных словах.

questions.question: What was strange about the instruction booklet?
questions.answer: It had no words, only drawings of a small man who had a terrible time.

questions.question: What mistake did the narrator make with the doors?
questions.answer: One door was upside down, so the handle was at the bottom.

questions.question: What happened when he did a victory dance?
questions.answer: He hit the wardrobe, it leaned forward, and a shelf fell on his foot.

questions.question: What did he do with the leftover screws?
questions.answer: He put them in a jar on a high shelf.
